To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed the first kinetic data structure for maintaining a triangulated plane subdivision with near-quadratic number (i.e. $n^2$) of topological changes (insertion or deletion of an entire edge), and that each topological change can be processed in constant time.
we present a KDS that maintains a two-dimensional kinetic triangulation with near-quadratic number topological events and $O(\log{n})$ processing time for each topological event.

1) we present the first KDS for triangulation that achieves near-quadratic performance, 2) our KDS has the smallest number of topological event for a triangulation, and 3) our KDS can be extended to maintain a triangulated surface with near-cubic topological events, the smallest number of such events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of kinetic data structures (KDSs) for dynamic geometric problems, which maintain the solution to a problem in the presence of continuous motions of geometric objects.
maintaining a triangulation of moving points with a small number (quadratic) of topological events and small (logarithmic) time per event.
the problem of maintaining a kinetic triangulation of a moving set of points in the Euclidean plane, where the points are allowed to move along algebraic trajectories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present the first KDS for maintaining triangulations that processes near-quadratic number topological events.
our KDS processes $n^k 2^{O((\sqrt{\log k}+\sqrt{\log n})\cdot \log\sqrt{\log n}\cdot \sqrt{\log\log n}+\sqrt{\sqrt{\log k}\log\sqrt{\\log n}})}$ topological events with probability 1 - o(1).
our KDS is the first known to process $n^2$ topological events with near-optimal $O(\log^2n)$ amortized time per event.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the number of topological changes in the triangulation of n moving points in the plane can be reduced from the worst case $\Omega(n^4)$ [1] to $n^2\cdot 2^{\tilde{O}(\sqrt{\log{n}})}$ with high probability.
we have developed a kinetic triangulation with near-quadratic number topological events, which is the best result known so far.
we have designed and implemented a KDS that maintains a triangulation in a dynamic environment with a small number topological events, which is the first KDS with such a guarantee.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a kinetic data structure can process near-quadratic number topological events with near-quadratic time per event, and that the KDS is robust with respect to the number of moving points.
the number of topological changes in a kinetic triangulation can be reduced significantly if we allow near-quadratic number changes.
a near-quadratic bound on topological events can hold for triangulations with near-linear number of vertices, which is the case for our KDS.
